name: Hotjar
whatYouLose: Scalable session storage and playback at volume
Aggregated heatmaps across thousands of sessions with sampling
Built-in PII masking that has been audited
Surveys and feedback widgets tied to recordings
prompt:
Build session replay and click heatmaps, a lightweight Hotjar replacement.

Stack: rrweb for recording and playback, Node + Hono, SQLite for metadata, gzipped event chunks on disk.
Features:
- Snippet that records sessions with rrweb, masks all inputs and any element with data-private, and uploads chunks every 10 seconds.
- Sample rate setting (e.g. record 10% of sessions).
- Dashboard: session list with duration, pages, device; player with skip-inactivity.
- Click heatmap per URL: aggregate click coordinates normalized to element selectors and overlay them on a screenshot iframe.
- Retention: delete recordings older than 30 days.
Done when: I can record my own visit to a demo page and replay it.
notes: rrweb does the hard recording work. Storage costs and privacy compliance at scale are what you are actually paying for.
